title: Natural common first-residue comparison of internal derived scalar functors
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l in universe u, and X any scheme in universe u. Use the actual continuous integral and first-quotient ring objects and derived reduction of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], the constant coefficient scalar and quotient maps of [def-sfb-integral-models-stacks-data], and the inverse integral point comparison of [def-sfb-integral-constant-model-realization]. There exists an isomorphism e from the continuous condensed first residue ring to the constant condensed first residue ring such that the following functors on the unbounded derived category of actual continuous integral modules are naturally isomorphic: first restrict along the inverse integral point comparison, then along the constant-to-continuous integral map, then derive extension along the constant first quotient; or first apply the actual derivedReduction at index zero and then restrict along the pullback of e inverse. There is no Noetherian, constructibility, Tor-amplitude, boundedness, or completeness hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary first-residue comparison to obtain the residue ring isomorphism e, flatness of the combined integral scalar map a, and the natural ordinary tensor isomorphism. Combine the two exact integral restriction functors using comapComp and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso.

Flat scalar restriction preserves native K-flat complexes. Identify native K-flatness with preservation of acyclicity by total tensor, then use the internal-section tensor comparison. The section-module comap and regular-module isomorphisms identify the restricted regular module and restriction functor with their ordinary sheaf-module counterparts. Flat scalar restriction preserves K-flatness there; transport back through the same comparisons.

Every internal complex admits a quasi-isomorphic native K-flat resolution. On this resolving class both scalar-extension computation counits are invertible, by the preceding restriction result on the left and native K-flatness on the right. Exact scalar restrictions have invertible localization factors on every complex. Apply resolving_square_iso to the termwise ordinary tensor comparison and these four computation transformations. Its descended natural isomorphism, composed with the integral restriction composition isomorphism, is exactly the asserted pair of derived functors.

lean.statement:
theorem internal_first_residue_reduction_comparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ e : Mon.mk (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E 1) ≅
        Mon.mk (IntegralModelsStacks.discreteObj (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1)),
      Nonempty
        ((Mod.comap (coefficientMap
            (IntegralConstantModel.pointComparison l E).inv.hom X)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          IntegralModelsStacks.restriction l E X ⋙
          (Mod.extendScalars (IntegralModelsStacks.residueMap l E X)).leftDerivedFunctor ≅
        AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X 0 ⋙
          (Mod.comap (coefficientMap e.inv.hom X)).mapDerivedCategory)
